display.purpose: The Owner's name and Page titles.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the Facts panel's role line.

title.purpose: Role titles (the Role entry's), panel titles, list rows and the Footer's title.

lede.purpose: The supporting line under a Page title, in secondary ink, 52ch measure.

body.purpose: Summaries and supporting lines in secondary ink, 68ch measure; also the value in a Text field, so Safari on iPhone doesn't zoom on focus; and, at the control weight (600) in full ink, a Facts panel fact's value and a Role entry's company.

small.purpose: Captions, notes, metadata (such as a Role entry's location and work model) and a field's hint in muted ink, and a field's error message; row links, controls and field labels at the control weight (600).

label.purpose: Martian Mono for stat labels (the Facts panel's) and dates (a Role entry's period), uppercase, 0.08em; chips and code set as-is.

about-me-display.purpose: Big Shoulders Display 900, uppercase, sized 24cqi so the Page title runs the band's width; Display colour.

about-me-headline.purpose: Big Shoulders Display 900, uppercase: Section titles in the Display colour.

about-me-title.purpose: Big Shoulders Display 800, uppercase: billing categories in the band's two key colours, item titles and the Footer's title.

about-me-billing.purpose: Archivo 800, uppercase: the items of a lineup, in the band's ink. --text-billing is named in both sets; the title size on the Portfolio.

about-me-lede.purpose: One line under the Page title, 52ch measure.

about-me-body.purpose: Stories and notes in the band's ink, 68ch measure.

about-me-small.purpose: 400: notes and a field's hint; controls and error messages take it at the control weight (700).

about-me-label.purpose: Archivo 800, 0.06em: labels, the language toggle, the Top bar's Pages, the Footer's links and band links, uppercase through --case-label; chips and code set as-is, because token names are case-sensitive. No monospace on About me.

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: Floating surfaces only (menus, popovers). Ring: ink 6% on paper, bone 30% on night. Shadow: ink 22% on paper, black 60% on night, the one non-ink colour, because no ink is darker than the night ground; the ring keeps floats legible there.

shadows.name: about-me-shadow-float
shadows.purpose: About me: a solid 3px ring in the band's ink, no shadow and no blur (--shadow-color is transparent).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Controls, row links, switch options. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Panel hover edge and wash. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-theme
motion.purpose: Theme crossfade of every token at once, except the theme switch, which only slides its pressed fill. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-spin
motion.purpose: One turn of the loading ring, on ease-linear. 0ms under reduced motion, where the ring fades instead.

motion.name: duration-pulse
motion.purpose: One fade of the loading ring under reduced motion, which replaces its turn. Kept under reduced motion: the one animation left there, with no movement.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only transition easing: exponential ease-out, no bounce.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The loading ring's fade under reduced motion, which runs both ways.

motion.name: ease-linear
motion.purpose: The loading ring's turn, the one loop.

motion.name: press-offset
motion.purpose: How far a pressed control sinks: both Buttons and the action Link, never the plain Link. 0px under reduced motion.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: How far a link's arrow moves on hover, focus and press. About me sets 3px. 0px under reduced motion.

motion.name: pulse-opacity
motion.purpose: The loading ring's faintest point as it fades under reduced motion.

states.name: focus-ring
states.purpose: Every focusable element.

states.name: disabled
states.purpose: Every disabled control.

states.name: indicator-width
states.purpose: The stroke of a loading ring; About me sets it to 3px.

states.name: error

states.name: line-width
states.purpose: Every hairline.

states.name: error-line-width

states.name: error-line-style
states.purpose: The error line's style; About me sets it to dashed, and the Portfolio turns it dashed in forced colours.

states.name: error-weight

states.name: error-forced-colors

states.name: about-me-focus-ring

states.name: about-me-error
states.purpose: About me: fields in error, with a Small message at the control weight (--error-weight); never a hue.

states.name: about-me-line-width
states.purpose: About me: every rule, outline and border.

states.name: about-me-indicator-width
states.purpose: About me: the loading ring's stroke, matching its rules.

states.name: link-hover-line
states.purpose: A link's hover, focus and press line, and a Top bar Page's or Footer link's hover and press line; the Portfolio changes colour only.

components.name: Panel Grid Cell
components.description: The Portfolio's collections as hairline cells that share their borders (About me never shows one). One column by default; a page sets its columns and fills every row, since an empty track shows the hairline as a solid block. Each cell holds a title, an optional note or other content, and a row link (a Link, the action variant where the cell carries the view's one filled action) pushed to its foot. Hover and focus within take the Wash and an inset Hairline Hover edge (in forced colours the lines take CanvasText and a hovered or focused cell a 2px inset Highlight outline); active is the row link pressed, which always comes with the cell's hover or focus within, so the active cell looks like the hovered one; no disabled. panel-grid.js moves focus between the row links with the arrow keys, by rendered position. Built in prototype/components/panel-grid/.

components.name: Facts Panel
components.description: Home's 30-second read in a hairline panel, and the Portfolio's only (About me never shows one): the role and seniority open it as one large line in the Headline role and the Display colour, on a hairline; then facts such as location and work model side by side at their content's width, each a label over a value in Body at the control weight; then the core technologies as Chips. The lead's label is for screen readers only, visually hidden but kept in the dl, since a visible label above the role line would read as an eyebrow and the role line names itself (the Owner's choice); the other labels stay visible, in the Label role in Muted Ink with tabular numerals. Every word, labels included, is Content. The Owner chose this form over a label-beside-value list and a grid of cells. Static: no states. Needs the Chip. Built in prototype/components/facts-panel/.

components.name: Role Entry
components.description: One role on Experience, and the Portfolio's only (About me never shows one). On narrow screens the head (the title, a heading at the level the page needs, and the company), the meta (period, location, work model) and the body (summary, achievements, Chips) stack in that order, 0.75rem apart, so the meta never sits above the title as an eyebrow. From 44rem the meta takes a side column (--role-entry-side-width, 12rem) down both rows, beside the head and then the body, 0.75rem by 2rem apart. The meta is Small in Muted Ink, one item per line, 0.5rem apart; only the period takes the Label role (monospace, uppercase, tabular numerals), while location and work model stay in the sans, as the Facts panel sets them. The title is in the Title role, the company 0.25rem under it in Body at the control weight, the summary and achievements in Body in Secondary Ink at the measure (a disc list with Muted Ink markers), then the technologies as Chips. Every part is required, as the Vision lists them for every role; the layout still holds when the location, work model, achievements or technologies are missing, so a gap never breaks it. Consecutive .role-entry siblings share a Hairline with 2rem above and below it, so a page that wraps entries in list items keeps them siblings or moves the rule to the item. Every word is Content except the dates' month names and "present", which follow the chosen language. The Owner chose a side column over a stacked entry and a hairline panel per role, and only the period in monospace over an all-monospace column. Static: no states. Needs the Chip. Built in prototype/components/role-entry/.

components.name: Lineup
components.description: About me's billing rows, and About me's only (the Portfolio never shows one), shown on the lime band: the wrapper sets every token the sample reads to the lime band's resolved values, so it renders standalone, and the lineup takes everything from tokens. Two 3px rules in Key close the list; each row stacks a category (display face, Title role, uppercase) over an item (Billing type in the band's ink), 0.5rem apart, in one column a long word breaks inside rather than widens, and from 36rem sets them in a --lineup-category-width (9rem) column and the rest on a shared baseline. Odd rows take Key and even rows Key Alt through --row-key. An item is a link only when the Owner gives it an address and then rests on a thin underline (--lineup-rest-line-width, 1px) in its row's key colour, thickening to the line width (3px) on hover, focus and press (a pressed item looks like a hovered one); focus adds the 3px ring. A plain item has no underline and no hover. No disabled. Built in prototype/components/lineup/.

narrative.overview:
The Portfolio's Visual language is a dark, confident engineering page where bold, tightly tracked type and hairline panels carry the authority and the facts lead. The Owner stays in the background: a small, plain photo beside the name, never a portrait as the centrepiece.

The Portfolio's Visual language is monochrome bone and ink. Dark is the default, always: a near-black ground carries warm bone ink. The complete light theme puts the same ink on bone paper and appears only when the visitor picks it in the dark and light switch, never from the system preference. Every colour token resolves both themes through `light-dark()`, so the active colour scheme picks one. Secondary text, metadata, hairlines and tints are the ink itself at fixed alpha steps; there is no hued accent anywhere. The primary action is the ink, filled; focus is an ink ring. The only hue in the system is error.

About me has its own, entirely distinct Visual language. It restyles the shared navigation, language toggle and Footer through tokens alone; their place and behavior never change.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default, always; light a complete equal the visitor switches to; both WCAG 2.2 AA.
Monochrome: bone ink on near-black, ink on bone paper, secondary ink and hairlines by alpha steps of the ink.
No hued accent: the primary action is filled ink, every other button is outlined in a hairline, row links are unboxed text, focus is an ink ring.
Bold display grotesk with tight tracking; monospace only for labels, tags, chips and numerals.
Hairline-bordered panel grids whose cells share borders, instead of cards and shadows.
Facts over the person: a hairline facts panel leads Home, the photo stays small.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Action Rule
rules.body: There is no accent colour. The primary action is the ink filled, with the ground as its text: one per view. Secondary buttons are outlined in Hairline Control; row links stay unboxed. Focus is an ink ring. If a view needs colour to show what to do next, the hierarchy is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The Alpha Steps Rule
rules.body: Secondary, muted, hairline and tint colours are always the ink mixed toward transparent at their fixed steps (84, 64, 26, 22, 10, 7, 4), and the Wash is the ink at 2% mixed into the ground; never new greys. The exceptions are few and named: input borders, set per theme to hold 3:1 (52% ink on paper, 44% bone on night); the raised surfaces (Night Raised, Paper Raised); and the float shadow, whose ring and shadow are the ink at 6% and 22% on paper and bone at 30% over black at 60% on night, because no ink is darker than the night ground.

rules.name: The Only Hue Is Error Rule
rules.body: Error is the sole hued colour, and it appears only where something went wrong.

rules.name: The Two Equal Themes Rule
rules.body: Every colour token exists in both themes and passes AA in both; dark is designed first, never light inverted.

rules.name: The Mono Labels Rule
rules.body: Monospace sets labels, tags, chips and numerals, never sentences or headings, and never as an eyebrow above a heading: the heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Hairline Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Reach for a hairline or a tint step first; a shadow is the last resort and only for something floating above the page.

dos: Do design the dark theme first and keep the light theme a complete equal, both at WCAG 2.2 AA.
Do open every Page in dark; show light only after the visitor picks it in the switch.
Do make the one primary action per view filled ink, and outline every other button in a hairline.
Do derive every secondary, muted, hairline and tint colour from the ink at its fixed alpha step.
Do lead Home with the facts in a hairline panel (role, seniority, location, work model, technologies) and keep the Owner's photo small and plain beside the name.
Do take every visual value from tokens, so About me can restyle the shared navigation, language toggle and Footer through tokens alone.
Do give every component all its states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, and loading, error or success where they apply) before it counts as done.
Do keep the Top bar's Pages and Toggles visible at every width: wrap the Toggles under the Pages rather than hide them in a menu.
Do move a Toggle's pressed fill to the option pressed next by sliding one indicator, not by fading between options.

Do keep motion to short expo ease-out transitions (150ms for controls, 200ms for panels, 240ms for the theme crossfade), no bounce, and 0ms under reduced motion. The one loop is the loading ring, on the linear ease (`--ease-linear`); under reduced motion nothing moves, and the ring alone fades instead of turning.
donts: Don't introduce a hued accent, a gradient or a multi-colour palette; the Owner turned down every one offered.
Don't use error red for anything but errors.
Don't follow the system colour scheme preference; the Owner chose dark always by default.
Don't build a template portfolio: no avatar hero, no skill pills, no grid of identical project cards.
Don't set a monospace eyebrow above a heading, or monospace prose.
Don't put a name or logo in the Top bar; the Owner chose a bar of Pages and Toggles only.
Don't let anything come before the repository link in the Footer but its title.
Don't set a Portfolio list as a Lineup; it is About me's only.
Don't make the Owner's photo a centrepiece: no large portrait, no colour effects, no full-bleed photo.
Don't put a shadow on anything that doesn't float above the page.
Don't give a field a placeholder, on either Visual language; the hint carries any example.
Don't let expression cost the 30-second read: role, seniority, technologies, location, CV and contact stay findable at a glance.

aboutMe.overview:
About me's Visual language sets the Owner's interests, recommendations and studies like a gig poster: flat colour bands, one per Section, a condensed uppercase display that runs the band's width, and lists set as a poster's billing. It is loud and warm where the Portfolio is quiet, and it never looks like a social profile, a gamer costume, the Portfolio recoloured, or anything corporate or cold.

It loads over the Portfolio's tokens and redefines the same names, so the shared components take its look through tokens alone. Spacing and motion stay the Portfolio's, except a longer link nudge (3px), a wider chip gap (0.5rem) and a Toggle with no inset to clear its 3px rules. It has one theme and no photo. Each band sets every colour token itself, so a component inside a band takes that band's colours. Illustration is optional: the language works without it, and the first band reserves a slot for one.
keyCharacteristics: Four flat bands, purple, sunset orange, lime and charcoal, rotating one per Section.
One theme and no theme switch; no photo; the language toggle keeps its place.
Big Shoulders Display, condensed and uppercase, sized to the band's width; Archivo for everything else.
Lists as poster billing: the category in large display type in the band's two key colours, the item in heavy uppercase Archivo in the band's ink.
One ink per band at full strength, no alpha steps; 3px ink rules and square corners.
No shadows, no blur, no gradients, no neon; an error is a dashed ink rule and its message, never a hue.

rules.name: The One Band Per Section Rule
rules.body: Every Section owns one band, and the bands rotate purple, sunset, lime, charcoal. A component never sets a palette colour; it reads the tokens of the band it sits in.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Each band has one ink at full strength: secondary, muted, hairline, control and input colours are the ink itself, and tints are transparent. On sunset any alpha step below full ink drops under 4.5:1. Three lines take another colour: the lineup's block rules are in Key; a hovered edge (`--color-hairline-hover`, `--color-input-hover`, `--color-action-hover-edge`) is the Display colour; and underlines are 3px in Key or Key Alt, on hover and while held for the language toggle, whose focus already shows the 3px ring, in Key Alt on hover and press and in Key under the current one for the Top bar's Pages, on hover and while held for the Footer's links, on hover, focus and press for band links; and linked lineup items rest on a thin underline in their row's key colour that thickens to 3px on hover, focus and press.

rules.name: The Cream Is Large Rule
rules.body: Cream holds only 3.3:1 on sunset, so on the sunset ground it sets large type only: display, headlines, the billing keys and the Footer's title (1.375rem at 800). On the charcoal action fill it is the action's text, at 15:1.

rules.name: The No Error Hue Rule
rules.body: No single hue reads on all four bands, so error is the band's ink, drawn as a dashed rule with its message, never a colour alone.

rules.name: The Band-Wide Title Rule
rules.body: The Page title is sized from its container's width (24cqi, from 3.5rem to 20rem), so it runs the band's width like a poster's lettering.

rules.name: The Billing Rule
rules.body: A list is a lineup: the category in the display face at title size, large type, in the band's two key colours, alternating Key and Key Alt down the list; the item in heavy uppercase Archivo at billing size in the band's ink; two 3px rules in Key above and below. On sunset the keys are charcoal and cream, so half the categories share the ink and stand apart by face and size.

rules.name: The Printed Flat Rule
rules.body: Nothing on About me casts or blurs; separate with a 3px ink rule or a change of band.

dos: Do give every Section one band, rotating purple, sunset, lime and charcoal, with the bar and intro on purple and the Footer on the next band in the rotation.
Do let a component read its band's tokens; never set a palette colour on a component.
Do set text in the band's one ink at full strength, and cream only at large sizes on sunset.
Do size the Page title from its container so it runs the band's width, in Big Shoulders Display, uppercase.

Do set lists as billing: the category in large display type in the band's two key colours, the item in heavy uppercase Archivo; a linked item rests on a thin underline in its category colour that thickens on hover, focus and press.
Do mark an error with a dashed 3px ink rule and its message.
Do keep the language toggle in its place and leave the theme switch out.
Do make every band work without an illustration; the slot is optional.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a blur, a gradient or neon; the bands are flat and printed.
Don't step the ink down by alpha; on sunset every step below full ink falls under 4.5:1.
Don't give error a hue; no single hue reads on all four bands.
Don't let it look like a social profile (cards, counters, feeds), a gamer or childish costume, the Portfolio recoloured, or anything corporate or cold.
Don't use Dance Gavin Dance's artwork, lettering or logo; the poster grammar is an own version.
Don't add a photo or a second theme.
Don't round a corner unless the thing is truly round.
